title: "Energon": Unveiling Transformers from GPU Power and Thermal Side-Channels
problem: GPU power and thermal fluctuations leak architectural details of transformer models deployed in MLaaS environments, enabling extraction of layer counts and attention head information without physical access.
motivation: Security of proprietary transformer models in shared GPU deployments is critical as side-channel attacks remain largely unexplored.
method: Exploits temporal variations in GPU power consumption and thermal output via unprivileged access to extract architectural parameters; analyzes encoder/decoder layers and attention head counts through statistical power signatures.
key_novelty: First demonstration of GPU power and thermal side-channels to reverse-engineer transformer architecture details at user privilege level.
contributions: Novel power/thermal side-channel analysis against transformers
Extraction of encoder/decoder layer and attention head information
Black-box adversarial attack achieving >93% success rate using extracted architecture
Evaluation across multiple public language and vision transformer models

metrics.accuracy: 89% model family identification, 100% hyperparameter classification, 93% adversarial success
metrics.other: Works in single-process and noisy multi-process scenarios

limitations: Requires physical proximity to GPU power/thermal sensors; evaluation limited to public models; practical deployment assumes accessible monitoring interfaces.
